Ella: Quick sync 1010 I'm consolidating a small "short-form" troubleshooting guide for 429s/timeouts/context clipping. Draft PR on staging: snippets + repro steps + a short migration note for Retry-Mode header. Can folks skim?
Sam: happy to. Are we still recommending exponential backoff + full jitter as the default in our SDK examples?
Priya: yes. Also please add a tiny note for Dedicated customers: routing may transparently route to a variant (e.g., -fast vs -dense) when capacity is constrained. That affects token budgeting.
Kev: Eng-runtime: confirmed - variant names will be redwood-fast-1 / redwood-dense-1. I'll add an inline note about token limits.
Ella: Thx. I've put a minimal curl repro and a streaming example showing what a truncated stream looks like (X-Stream-Interrupted). Example curl: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-fast-1","prompt":"...","max_tokens":128,"variant":"redwood-fast-1"}'
```
Sam: Add a labeled "local stress repro" command for support: `heyload -n 150 -c 20 https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate` + note to capture X-RateLimit-Reset, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining.
Priya: SDK snippets: Python show client.generate_with_retry(backoff="exponential_jitter", max_retries=4) and JS show client.create({ retry: { mode: "exponential_jitter", maxRetries: 4 } }). Then a tiny mapping table to curl for debugging.
Kev: Runtime: service will set X-Context-Truncated when we evict older KV/prefix entries; add a troubleshooting bullet: "if you see X-Context-Truncated -> trim earlier turns or enable prefix caching".
Ella: Good call. I also added a one-paragraph migration blurb: old header X-Retry semantics -> new Retry-Mode header (server-side vs client-side). Needs an editorial pass.
CI-bot: Link-check job passed for docs-staging PR #6301 at 7098778900 :white_check_mark:
Sam: I'll tidy anchors and ensure the playbook links to the runbook. Also suggest adding a 4-step ascii flowchart for quick triage: 
1) Inspect X-RateLimit-* headers
2) Apply exponential backoff + jitter
3) Fallback to a compatible model variant
4) Contact support with request-id & sample payload
Priya: Minor nit: label the streaming example as "how a timeout looks (client-side)" and show header X-Stream-Interrupted: reason=timeout.
Kev: Left two inline comments about exact token caps for redwood-fast-1; eng-runtime will post numbers by tomorrow.
Ella: I'll address comments, backport the snippets to the 429 playbook page, and cut a follow-up PR adding the micro-migration table. ETA: EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
